Between the orange boxes are two opposing horizontal arrows: competition to trade, “Entry of new firms and competition dynamics drive ability to export”; trade to competition, “Trade in digital services can drive competition in importing countries.” Below are three purple policy panels, each connected by vertical arrows to the relevant outcome area: “Competition policy” lists “Adapt antitrust rules to challenges posed by data-driven businesses”; “Adopt pro-competition data remedies subject to safeguards for innovation”; “Ensure that traditional regulations promote competition and consumer choice.” “Tax policy” lists “Create a level playing field between digital and analog businesses”; “Adapt indirect tax administration to platform businesses”; “Adapt direct tax rules to account for intangible value drivers.” “Trade policy” lists “Establish regulatory framework for cross-border data flows”; “Balance individual rights, implementation costs, and business opportunities”; “Adopt international (trade) agreements for data.” The vertical policy connectors include downward orange arrows and upward purple arrows.
